summary: Enterprise finance customer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for chat + embeddings. Primary focus on audit logging and SIEM integration; strict data residency and KMS BYOK requirements.
crm_notes:
Sales/Discovery notes - shorthand and action items:
- 2026-01-15 intro call (Jordan + Maya) — they want private VPC with dedicated control plane in us-east-1; compliance for banking division.
- Main ask: comprehensive audit logging exported to Splunk/QRadar/Syslog + long retention. CISO emphasized: 'we need schema to match our SIEM, and tamper-evidence for logs'.
- SIEM export requirements: support push to HTTP(s) collector (CEF/JSON) OR S3 drop with event notifications. Must provide sample payloads.
- Log schema expectations: per-request fields: request_id, customer_id (hashed), model_version, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, user_agent, src_ip (anonymized), action (generate/stream/embeddings), error_code, matched_cache=True/False. They want a mapping sheet (we provided acacia-siem-schema.xlsx stub).
- Retention: legal requires 3 years for audit logs; security ops wants 1 year hot in SIEM + archived encrypted to S3 for 3 years. Need support for lifecycle rules and MFA delete.
- Access logs: audit of who accessed logs (read/export) – must be integrated with their SIEM and access-controlled via RBAC; logs should include actor, role, timestamp, operation.
- KMS: BYOK desired. Keys managed in customer AWS account (KMS key ARN provided in demo). Need documentation on key rotation, access policies, and cross-account grant model.
- Integrity & tamper-evidence: suggestion: sign log batches with HMAC and provide verification process. They asked about append-only storage options.
- PII/redaction: want token-level redaction config and policy hooks (redact on export). Need sample configs.
- Metric tagging: correlate cost and latency per-customer via request_id and token counters. They want token billing fields in logs.
- Integration tests requested: deliver sample SIEM payloads, S3 bucket policy template, CloudWatch/Syslog examples, and a short runbook for incident investigations.
- Quote from CISO: 'Cannot accept vendor logs that we cannot validate in our SIEM or that bypass our KMS.'
- Next demo (security deep-dive) scheduled for 2026-03-15 with infra + security.

detailed_requirements: SIEM export: support push to HTTP collector (JSON/CEF) and S3 drop with event notifications
Log schema: per-request canonical fields (request_id, model, route, tokens, latency, error_code, anonymized_src_ip, user_agent, customer_hash)
Retention: hot SIEM index 12 months (configurable), archived encrypted S3 3 years; legal wants ability to extend to 7 years upon request
Access logs: read/export operations must be logged with actor, role, timestamp, IP, and exported to SIEM
KMS integration: BYOK required, cross-account grants, support key rotation and access logging to their CloudTrail
Tamper-evidence: signed log batches (HMAC) and append-only storage recommendations
Data residency: all logs and archives must reside in us-east-1 under customer-controlled buckets
PII controls: configurable redaction on export, token-level scrubbing hooks before log emission
